lesson.title: Where did it go?

steps.headline: Displacement is final position minus initial position, and its sign shows the direction.

lead.text: Position is measured from an origin, a place you choose to call zero. You also choose which way is positive.
A move to larger positions is positive. A move to smaller positions is negative.
The dot starts at 2 m and finishes at 9 m. Right is positive.

reveal.text: You just used final minus initial: 9 − 2. The plus sign says the dot moved the positive way.

steps.headline: Distance is the total length of the path, so every stretch adds.

lead.text: Displacement only compares the ends. Distance follows the whole path, and it counts the trip back as well as the trip out.
Distance has no direction and is never negative.

steps.headline: A trolley goes from 1 m to 5 m, then back to 2 m. Find its displacement and its distance.

workedSteps.text: Displacement uses only the ends: finish minus start.
Distance adds the stretches. Out is 5 − 1.

steps.headline: A cart goes from 1 m to 7 m and back to 1 m. What distance does it cover?

workedSteps.text: The way out runs from 1 m to 7 m.
The way back is the same length.

lead.text: Two students watch the same trip. They measure from different origins, so their readings differ.

reveal.text: Moving the origin shifts both readings together. The gap between them is the displacement, and it stays put.

lead.text: A robot drives along a straight track, then turns round partway.

reveal.text: The robot's displacement is only +3 m, yet it covered 13 m. The turn makes the two numbers differ.

lesson.orientation: Distinguish a change in position from the total distance travelled.
lesson.nextAction: Try the next idea, then return for a fresh problem after a delay.

blocks.text: You walk 5 m east from your front door, then turn and walk 2 m back west.

intro.promise: By the end you'll tell a change in position from the distance travelled, and give the change a sign.
intro.whyItMatters: Every later idea about motion starts from where things are and how that changes.

recap.keyIdea: Displacement is final position minus initial position, with a sign. Distance adds every stretch of the path.

blocks.text: You found that 5 m out and 2 m back leaves you 3 m from the door. You also saw an out-and-back trip of 6 m each way cover 12 m while ending where it began.

recap.nextHook: Now add time: how fast does the position change?

questions.prompt: An object moves from x = 2 m to x = 9 m. With right positive, what is its displacement in metres?
hints: Locate the starting and finishing coordinates.
Subtract the start from the finish.
Calculate 9 − 2.
questions.onCorrect: +7 m. Final minus initial: the size is how far it moved and the plus sign says which way.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the two readings. Displacement is a difference: final minus initial.
The size is right, but the sign is not. It moved towards larger positions.

questions.prompt: A cart goes from 1 m to 7 m and back to 1 m. What total distance does it travel, in metres?
hints: Count both stretches of the trip.
Each stretch has length 7 − 1 metres.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: It travels 6 m out and 6 m back, for 12 m.

questions.onCorrect: 12 m. Distance adds every stretch of the path, so the trip back counts as well as the trip out.

misconceptions.feedback: That is how far the cart ended from where it began. Distance counts every stretch it travelled.
That is the trip out only. The cart also has to come back.

questions.prompt: The origin shifts so that a trip from 2 m to 9 m is recorded as 12 m to 19 m. What happens to the displacement?
hints: Compare the differences between the two pairs of endpoints.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Both readings increase by 10 m; their difference stays +7 m.

questions.onCorrect: It stays the same. Both readings rise by the same amount, so their difference does not change.

misconceptions.feedback: Only the readings change, not the trip. Both ends move by the same amount, so the gap between them does not grow.
Nothing in the trip doubled. Compare the gap between the two readings in each pair.

questions.prompt: A robot moves from 0 m to 8 m, then back to 3 m. How far does it travel altogether, in metres?
hints: Break the trip at the turning point.
The return stretch runs from 8 m to 3 m.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The path has lengths 8 m and 5 m: 8 + 5 = 13 m.

questions.onCorrect: 13 m. Break the trip at the turning point and add the two stretches.

misconceptions.feedback: That is how far the robot ended from where it began. The distance counts the whole path.
That is the trip out only. The robot also travels back.
That is the return stretch only. Count the trip out as well.

questions.prompt: A lift's marked position changes from 5 m to −4 m. With upward positive, find its displacement in metres.
hints: Keep the minus sign on the final position.
Subtract the initial position from the final position.
Calculate −4 − 5.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: Final minus initial gives −4 − 5 = −9 m, downward.

questions.onCorrect: −9 m. Final minus initial gives a negative number when the move is in the negative direction.

misconceptions.feedback: The size is right, but the lift went down. With upward positive, a downward move needs a minus sign.
That adds the two readings. Take the start away from the finish.

questions.prompt: A cart travels from −2 m to 4 m and then to 1 m. Which statement describes its trip?
hints: Use endpoints for displacement and both path lengths for distance.

answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Its displacement is 1 − (−2) = 3 m. Its distance is 6 + 3 = 9 m.

questions.onCorrect: Displacement compares the ends: 3 m. Distance adds both stretches: 9 m.

misconceptions.feedback: These are swapped. The ends give the displacement, and the whole path gives the distance.
The cart finishes at a larger position than it started, so its displacement is not negative.

questions.prompt: How far from the door are you, in metres?
hints: Draw the door as 0 and the first walk as a line going out.
The second walk goes back along the same line.
Take the 2 m back off the 5 m.
questions.onCorrect: 3 m. The second walk undid part of the first. Physics keeps track of position this way.

misconceptions.feedback: That adds the two walks. The second walk goes the other way, so it takes you back towards the door.

questions.prompt: A marker moves from 6 m to 2 m along a track, with right positive. What is its displacement in metres?
hints: Which reading is the finish, and which is the start?
Displacement is the finish minus the start.
Take the 6 away from the 2.
questions.onCorrect: −4 m. It moved towards smaller positions, so the displacement is negative.

misconceptions.feedback: The size is right, but the marker moved the negative way. The sign has to show that.
That adds the two readings. Displacement is a difference: finish minus start.

questions.prompt: A walker goes 4 m right, then 4 m left. What total distance does the walker cover, in metres?
hints: How long is each stretch?
Distance adds each stretch, pointing either way.
Add the two stretches.
questions.onCorrect: 8 m. Distance never cancels: every stretch adds to it, whichever way it points.

misconceptions.feedback: That is the net change in position. Distance counts both stretches.
That is one stretch. The walker covers two.

questions.prompt: Why does the 5 m turning point not appear in the displacement?
hints: Read each choice against the situation before you answer.

acceptedIdeas: Displacement compares only the start and the finish.
answerAuthority.exampleAnswer: Displacement compares only the start and the finish.

choices.label: Displacement compares only the start and the finish.
The trolley never really reached 5 m.
Turning points are always ignored in physics.

questions.onCorrect: Displacement depends on the two ends only. What happens in between does not change it.

misconceptions.feedback: It did reach 5 m: that is where it turned round. The question is why that point does not enter the sum.
Turning points matter for distance. They are only absent from displacement because of what displacement compares.

questions.prompt: A runner goes from −4 m to 2 m, then on to −3 m. What total distance does the runner cover, in metres?
hints: Break the run at the turning point.
The first stretch is from −4 m to 2 m.
Add 6 and the length of the second stretch.

answerAuthority.workedAnswer: The stretches are 6 m and 5 m: 6 + 5 = 11 m.

questions.onCorrect: 11 m. Split the run where it turns, then add the lengths of the two stretches.

misconceptions.feedback: That is how far the runner ended from the start. Distance counts the whole path.
That is the first stretch only. Add the stretch back.
